A new `WebFunction` component for AWS Lambda Web Functions, on version 7.54.0 of the AWS provider, and Cloudflare and Vercel API tokens kept out of the state. Still built on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

Thanks to [@mountain1009](https://github.com/mountain1009), who sent the `WebFunction` component and the provider update it needed, and to [@jl4nz](https://github.com/jl4nz), who sent the fix for copying in `sst dev`.

### ⚠️ Breaking changes

- **The AWS provider is now 7.54.0, with Pulumi 3.270.0.** If your `sst.config.ts` pins `aws` below 7.54.0, raise the pin or remove it; otherwise the CLI stops with `provider version too low`. The first deploy after upgrading replaces the provider entry, and nothing else. ([#233](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/233), by [@mountain1009](https://github.com/mountain1009))

### New

- **`sst.aws.WebFunction`, for [AWS Lambda Web Functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/web-functions.html).** It deploys a plain HTTP server, such as Hono or Express, on Node.js 24 behind an HTTPS endpoint: your code starts a server instead of exporting a handler. It supports links, `permissions` and IAM authorization. In `sst dev` the server runs on your machine, as a `Service` does. A deploy that changes the code or settings creates a new revision and moves the endpoint to it, keeping its URL. ([#103](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/103), by [@mountain1009](https://github.com/mountain1009); [anomalyco/sst#7038](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/issues/7038))
  - A deploy role with limited permissions needs the Lambda Web Functions actions, and `cloudformation:CreateResource` and `cloudformation:GetResourceRequestStatus`, because the provider creates the function through Cloud Control.
  - Lambda can report a revision as active before your server is listening, so call it after a deploy.

### Fixes

- **Cloudflare and Vercel API tokens are no longer written to the state.** SST's Cloudflare resources (DNS records, Workers and their assets, KV data, a Worker's URL and placement) and Vercel's DNS records took the API token as an input, so it was stored in plain text in the stage's state. They now use the credentials the CLI already has. Each of them updates once on its next deploy. A stage's earlier state versions still have the token: deploy or remove each stage with this version, then rotate the token. ([#228](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/228))
- **`sst dev` copies every line you selected,** including the ones scrolled out of view, not only the lines on screen. ([#232](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/232), by [@jl4nz](https://github.com/jl4nz))

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.24.0
```

To switch an existing project:

1. Check that `node --version` shows `v22` or later, wherever you run `sst`, CI included.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.24.0"` and reinstall.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. It still needs Node.js 22 or later, to run `sst.config.ts`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
